title: US Strikes IRGC Radar Site in Kermanshah, Killing 4 Aerospace Force Personnel
detail: CENTCOM launched a new wave of strikes against Iranian military targets on Tuesday, September 1, ending the recent pause and returning to active combat. One strike hit an IRGC Aerospace Force radar installation in Kermanshah province, western Iran; Iranian state media reported 4 IRGC Aerospace Force personnel killed. CENTCOM said the September 1 strikes targeted Iranian air-defense, radar, maritime, mine-laying, and communications facilities, and said they followed Iranian attacks on three oil tankers and on US forces and bases in the region. President Trump said the US hit 'an unspecified number of Iranian radars that Iran was attempting to rebuild.'

title: US Strikes IRGC Maritime and Mine-Laying Facility on Lavan Island, Killing 3 Basij Members
detail: As part of the same September 1 strike wave, US forces hit an IRGC maritime and mine-laying facility on Lavan Island in the Persian Gulf. Iranian state media reported 3 Basij paramilitary members killed at the site. CENTCOM described the broader Sept 1 target set as IRGC air-defense, radar, maritime, mine-laying, and communications facilities, framing the strikes as a response to Iranian attacks on oil tankers and US forces/bases in the region.

title: Iran Says US Strike Hit Wedding Gathering in Kuhestak, Killing Civilians; CENTCOM 'Looking Into' Claim
detail: Iran said a US strike hit a wedding celebration in the coastal town of Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, on September 1, accusing Washington of a 'war crime.' Iranian Red Crescent and state media reported 4-5 people killed, including a child, and 63-71 wounded, with injured civilians shown at a hospital in nearby Minab. US Central Command said it was 'looking into' the report but said the US military 'never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.' The claim remains disputed and unconfirmed by independent investigators.

title: Unclaimed Strikes Disable Saudi and Liberian-Flagged VLCCs Near Khasab, Exposing ~4M Barrels of Saudi Crude
detail: The Saudi-flagged VLCC Sidr (operated by Bahri) and the Liberian-flagged VLCC Senegal Prosperity (operated by South Korea's Sinokor Group) were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting near Khasab, Oman, at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz. Senegal Prosperity took three projectiles to its port-side engine room and ballast tank, went dead in the water, lost shipboard communications, and was left listing; its crew was evacuated by local authorities. Both vessels had loaded roughly 2 million barrels of Saudi crude each at the Ju'aymah terminal, exposing about 4 million barrels combined. No crew casualties were reported. CENTCOM cited attacks on oil tankers and on US forces/bases as the trigger for its September 1 counterstrikes on Iranian territory.

title: IAEA: No Verification Access to Iran Since Feb 28, Uranium Stockpile 'a Matter of Proliferation Concern'
detail: The IAEA reported it has conducted no verification activities in Iran under the NPT safeguards agreement since the war began on February 28, has been denied access to 20 declared nuclear sites plus one additional location, and has not received required reporting on the status of nuclear material or design information — including at the repeatedly-struck Isfahan enrichment plant. Iran's Atomic Energy Organization chief Mohammad Eslami said the agency cannot inspect sites hit by military strikes until new inspection protocols are developed. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi called the lack of information on Iran's nuclear material 'a matter of proliferation concern' and reiterated that only a 'long-lasting, verifiable diplomatic agreement' can resolve the standoff. The report will be discussed at the IAEA Board of Governors meeting September 21-25.
